# References


# Import and transform

## Regional inequality data

```{r}
regions<- read_dta("regions-data.dta")
head(regions)
```

```{r}
summary(regions) # Can we redo this by year?
```


- It is a unbalanced plong panel format covering years 1992-2012
- In the year 2012, there are 3,124 regions
- In the year 2002, there are 3,136 regions
- In the year 1992, there are 2,969 regions

- The authors claim that their final dataset is based on 180 countries and 3166 regions 
- From the shape file, the GADM data has 3610 observation at level 1


```{r}
ine<- read_dta("Data/Main_Data.dta") %>% 
  mutate(iso_a3 = Country_ISO) # useful for merging datasets
head(ine)
```


```{r}
ine1992 <- ine %>% 
  filter(year == 1992)
ine1992
```



```{r}
ine2012 <- ine %>% 
  filter(year == 2012)
ine2012
```


```{r}
ine1992_2012 <- ine %>% 
  group_by(iso_a3) %>% 
  summarise(mean_gini =mean(GINIW_pred_GDP_pc))
ine1992_2012
```


```{r}
ine1992_2001 <- ine %>% 
  filter(year < 2002) %>% 
  group_by(iso_a3) %>% 
  summarise(mean_gini_1992_2001 =mean(GINIW_pred_GDP_pc))
ine1992_2001
```


```{r}
ine2002_2012 <- ine %>% 
  filter(year > 2001) %>% 
  group_by(iso_a3) %>% 
  summarise(mean_gini_2002_2012 =mean(GINIW_pred_GDP_pc))
ine2002_2012
```


```{r}
convergence <- inner_join(ine1992_2001, ine2002_2012, by = "iso_a3" ) %>% 
  mutate(gini_difference = mean_gini_1992_2001 - mean_gini_2002_2012 ) # So, a + sings means convergence
convergence 
```
 
 



## SF (Shapefile) of the world

```{r}
data(World) # from the tmap package
map <- World
map
```


# Merge datasets

```{r}
map_and_ine1992 <- inner_join(map, ine1992, by = "iso_a3")
map_and_ine2012 <- inner_join(map, ine2012, by = "iso_a3")
map_and_ine1992_2012 <- inner_join(map, ine1992_2012, by = "iso_a3")
map_and_convergence <- inner_join(map, convergence, by = "iso_a3")
```


# Regional inequality

From the paper

![](Figures/Figure_2.jpg)

- The figure shows the population-weighted gini coeffient for the  period 1992-2012. This is a multiyear average
- Darker colors represent higher levels of inequality


```{r}
summary(map_and_ine1992_2012$mean_gini)
```


```{r}
tm_shape(map_and_ine1992_2012) +
  tm_polygons("mean_gini",
              breaks = c(0.011, 0.037, 0.62, 0.85, 0.148),   # ERROR: These breaks are not working
              title = "Regional Gini \n 1992-2012",
              style = "pretty",   
              palette = "Reds", 
              id = "name", 
              popup.var= TRUE,
              colorNA = NULL) +
  tm_text("iso_a3", 
          size = "AREA") +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE)
```



```{r}
summary(map_and_ine1992$GINIW_pred_GDP_pc)
```



```{r}
tm_shape(map_and_ine1992) +
  tm_polygons("GINIW_pred_GDP_pc",
              breaks = c(-Inf, 0.003, 0.037, 0.62, 0.85, 0.148, Inf),   # ERROR: These breaks are not working
              title = "Regional Gini 1992",
              style = "pretty",   
              palette = "Reds", 
              id = "name",

              colorNA = NULL) +

```



# Regional convergence


- Countries displayed in green experienced convergence and countries displayed in red experienced an increase in inequality. The darker the color, the larger the change.

- At least one-quarter of the countries experience divergence


![](Figures/Figure_3.jpg)


```{r}
#fromThePaper <- c(0.003, 0.037, 0.62, 0.85, 0.148)

tm_shape(map_and_convergence) +
  tm_polygons("gini_difference",
              title = "Convergence \n 1992-2012",
              style = "pretty",   
              palette = "RdYlGn", 
              id = "name", 
              popup.var= TRUE,
              colorNA = NULL) +
  tm_text("iso_a3", 
          size = "AREA") +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE)
```
